Sportsmail will give you all the details for every Barclays Premier League match, including team updates, possible lineups, betting odds, and Opta statistics. Here is the information for Aston Villa’s home game against QPR.

**Aston Villa vs. Queens Park Rangers (at Villa Park)**

**Team News:**
Aston Villa manager Tim Sherwood cannot use three important players for this match against QPR. Alan Hutton hurt his ankle during Saturday’s 3-1 loss to Manchester United and will miss Tuesday’s game. Scott Sinclair and Ashley Westwood are also out.

Kim Sei-young will start the final round of the ANA Inspiration with a three-shot lead. On Saturday in California, she shot a score of 69, which is three strokes under par.

Kim, who is from South Korea, was leading by two shots at the halfway point at Mission Hills Country Club. She made a birdie on the first hole, but a bogey on the fifth hole stopped her progress. She got back to one stroke under par for the day when she made a bogey on the ninth hole. Then, she made birdies on the 16th and 17th holes. This brought her score to three under par for the day and 10 under par overall.

Colin Montgomerie says that while Tiger Woods is trying to win the Masters, it would be a disaster for everyone if Woods leaves the tournament with a limp. Woods recently announced he is returning to competitive golf for the first time since early February. He had to withdraw from the first round of the Farmers Insurance Open because of a back injury. Woods is currently ranked 104th in the world and has not played in any official tournaments. His only recent practice has been in Florida and at Augusta over the past few days, so it is unclear how well he will perform. The former world number one confirmed earlier this week that he will play in the Masters.

A year ago, Liverpool’s attack was strong and fast. Luis Suarez and Daniel Sturridge were playing very well together. They scored 52 of the team’s 101 Premier League goals.

This season, the team has not scored as many goals. It was always going to be very hard to replace Suarez. However, fans hoped the rest of the team was good enough to make up for his absence.

Unfortunately, manager Brendan Rodgers has not been able to get the attack working like it did last season.

The Miami Open is turning into a week of big celebrations. Serena Williams recently won her 700th career match, and the tournament honored her with a large cake. This happened the day after Andy Murray’s 500th win, which was also marked with a huge cake.

Williams reached the semi-finals by beating Germany’s Sabine Lisicki with scores of 7-6, 1-6, and 6-3. However, she will not play her sister, Venus, because Venus lost to Spain’s Carla Suarez Navarro. Despite this, the world’s top-ranked player, Serena, is determined to keep playing in what is the closest thing to a home tournament for her. The text also notes that Serena posed next to her cake after reaching this milestone.

Andy Murray has a clear message for other British tennis players who are upset about Aljaz Bedene joining them: stop complaining. Instead, Murray thinks they should use Bedene’s presence as motivation to improve their own game. Bedene, who is originally from Slovenia, is currently ranked number 83 in the world.

Right now, any complaints are being kept private. The issue is also less serious because Bedene is not allowed to play for the British Davis Cup team. However, this could change if the International Tennis Federation allows his appeal to compete. Bedene was recently shown in photos at his British citizenship ceremony in Hatfield on Tuesday morning.

On Friday, during the second round of the ANA Inspiration golf tournament, South Korea’s Kim Sei-young made a great score on the final hole. The 18th hole is a "par five," meaning it usually takes five shots to finish. Kim hit her second shot very well, landing it just six feet from the hole, and then made the putt. This gave her a score of 65, which is seven strokes under par.

This amazing play put Kim in the lead by two shots. She is now at seven strokes under par (137 total). The previous leader, Morgan Pressel, shot a 72, so she is now two shots behind Kim.

Kim is 22 years old. She won her first LPGA Tour title in

Nick Scholfield will ride Spring Heeled, owned by Jim Culloty, in the Grand National at Aintree on April 11.

Scholfield was originally expected to ride Sam Winner, a horse trained by Paul Nicholls. However, Sam Winner was stopped during the Cheltenham Gold Cup, so it is not sure if he will run in the Grand National.

Nicholls decided to let Scholfield ride Spring Heeled instead. He said it would be unfair to force Scholfield to ride a horse that might not even run, especially when another strong contender was available.

Defending champion Novak Djokovic narrowly avoided an upset against Alexandr Dolgopolov to reach the quarter-finals of the Miami Open. Dolgopolov, who was unseeded and ranked 65th in the world (64 spots lower than Djokovic), surprised the Serbian by winning the first set tie-break and taking a 4-2 lead in the second set. However, Djokovic recovered his composure, forced a deciding third set, and won it easily as his opponent’s energy faded. Djokovic celebrated after securing his spot in the quarter-finals on Tuesday.

The Newport Gwent Dragons won a close match against the Cardiff Blues with a final score of 25-21. This win allowed the Dragons to reach the semi-finals of the European Challenge Cup.

The Dragons were behind for most of the game but came back to win. They scored tries through wing Hallam Amos, substitute Nic Cudd, and a penalty try. Tom Prydie and Dorian Jones also scored penalties, and Prydie kicked two successful conversions.

The Cardiff Blues scored tries through scrum-half Lloyd Williams, fly-half Gareth Anscombe, and number eight Josh Navidi. Anscombe also kicked three successful conversions. The image shows substitute Nic Cudd scoring a try for the Dragons at Rodney Parade.

A kangaroo from Australia escaped and was seen hopping around in West Germany, surprising people who watched. Police in Rhein Erft got a strange phone call saying a big kangaroo was happily hopping through a field. At first, they thought it was an April Fool’s joke and ignored the call. Later, they realized the report was real and found the Australian animal in a field in Bruhl.

Channel 7 accidentally showed a funny name on the screen during a major Australian charity event. The TV hosts didn’t realize that a donor named Hugh G. Rection had given $32.38. This small donation got his name on the screen, and people on Twitter quickly noticed the mistake.

Despite the error, the Royal Children’s Hospital’s Good Friday Appeal raised over $17.1 million. This money will help with important research and facilities for young patients. This amount is higher than the $16.8 million raised last year.

On Tuesday at Key Biscayne, Spain’s Carla Suarez Navarro beat three-time Miami Open champion Venus Williams with scores of 0-6, 6-1, and 7-5. Suarez Navarro had a terrible first set but came back to win. This victory set up a semi-final match against Germany’s ninth seed, Andrea Petkovic.

Petkovic reached the last four by defeating the 14th-seeded Czech player, Karolina Pliskova, with scores of 6-4 and 6-2. Williams dominated the first set, beating Suarez Navarro 6-0 in less than half an hour. However, Suarez Navarro regrouped and fought back impressively. The image shows Venus Williams looking frustrated as she loses to Suarez Navarro in the Miami Open

Alfonso Thomas, Somerset’s new limited-overs captain, has agreed to coach the Delhi Daredevils in the Indian Premier League this month. Thomas, an experienced fast bowler, is still recovering from a broken ankle and is not yet ready to play in Somerset’s first County Championship match against Durham. With Somerset’s permission, he is free to take on this short-term coaching role with Delhi until April 16.

Bath is counting on its England players to lead the team against Leinster in Dublin. They want to make up for losing to Ireland 19-9 at the Aviva Stadium last month. George Ford, Dave Attwood, Jonathan Joseph, and Anthony Watson are all playing again in the place where they lost. That loss stopped England’s chance to win the Grand Slam. Bath’s head coach thinks that defeat might actually help them in their Champions Cup quarter-final. Jonathan Joseph will be one of the England players at Bath in Dublin on Saturday. He has a point to prove after England’s loss in Dublin during the Six Nations.

Andy Murray almost had more time to prepare for his wedding next week, but he still has tennis to finish first. He is now in the semi-finals of the Miami Open. He had a difficult match against 21-year-old Austrian Dominic Thiem. Thiem tied the second set at 4-4, but Murray won the match 3-6, 6-4, 6-1 in one hour and 45 minutes. Murray is now waiting to see who wins the other semi-final match between Tomas Berdych and Juan Monaco from Argentina. Before this tournament, Thiem lost in the second round of a smaller event to Aljaz Bedene, who is soon becoming a British citizen.

Sim Bhullar and the Sacramento Kings are about to make history in the NBA. The Kings are signing Bhullar to a 10-day contract, which will make him the first player of Indian descent in the league, according to someone who knows about the deal. This person spoke to the Associated Press anonymously because the Kings do not plan to announce the signing until Thursday. The announcement will happen when another player’s 10-day contract ends and a spot opens up on the team. Bhullar, who is 7 feet 5 inches tall and weighs 360 pounds, is being called up from the Reno Bighorns, the Kings’ minor league team.

Rangers manager Stuart McCall has been told that removing the club from the London Stock Exchange will not hurt the team’s chances of getting promoted. Fans were shocked on Thursday when the club was removed from the AIM market because Dave King, who is about to become chairman, could not find a new advisor. Interim chairman Paul Murray blamed the old board for the decision but tried to calm worries by saying the new leaders are looking into moving to a different market called ISDX. The paragraph also notes that Stuart McCall was seen managing his players during a training session on Good Friday.

Moeen Ali is expected to join the England team for the final part of their Test series in the West Indies, as his side injury gets better. He was hurt during England’s unsuccessful World Cup campaign, so he was not included in the squad for the Caribbean. Moeen was injured while playing against New Zealand during the World Cup. However, he had a great start to his Test cricket career last summer, taking 22 wickets in seven matches.

Manager Arsene Wenger believes Arsenal is back on track, and everyone can sense it. On Saturday, Arsenal beat Liverpool 4-1 at home. This was their seventh straight win in the Premier League, moving them up to second place.

Manchester City could take second place if they beat Crystal Palace on Monday. Chelsea is still seven points ahead of Arsenal, so winning the title is unlikely. However, when all of Arsenal’s players are available, they can compete with any team.

Tottenham manager Mauricio Pochettino believes goalkeeper Michel Vorm has the mental strength to move past his disappointment in the Capital One Cup final and perform well as a backup to Hugo Lloris. Lloris is out with a knee injury, so Vorm will start for Tottenham against Burnley on Sunday at Turf Moor. The 31-year-old, who joined Tottenham from Swansea this summer, sat on the bench during last month’s League Cup final loss to Chelsea, even though he had played in earlier rounds. Vorm is now set to replace Lloris for Sunday’s match.

Celtic striker Leigh Griffiths ate a Tunnock’s Tea Cake during the warm-up for a match against St Mirren on Good Friday. He looked around nervously before unwrapping the snack within the first 10 minutes of the game. This action goes against manager Ronnie Deila’s rules, which require players to follow a strict diet to stay in top physical condition. Griffiths was seen eating the biscuit on the substitutes' bench during the opening part of the match.

Porto has made £440 million from selling players over the last 11 years, following the confirmation that Danilo will join Real Madrid this summer. Since winning the Champions League in 2004 under manager Jose Mourinho, the club has regularly sold players for large profits. Most of these sales involve South American players, partly because Portugal’s work permit rules are more flexible for Brazilians. Danilo, a Brazilian defender who plays for Porto, will move to Real Madrid for £23 million. The text also notes that Jose Mourinho celebrated winning the 2004 Champions League with Porto.

Lionel Messi’s swollen foot is still a worry for Barcelona. He missed two games for Argentina during the break, and now he must undergo tests to see if he can play against Celta Vigo on Sunday.

The Spanish newspaper SPORT put Messi on its front cover, saying the four-time Ballon d’Or winner wants to play as his team tries to win the La Liga title. However, tests on Thursday might change those hopes. Teammate Gerard Pique was optimistic about Messi playing, but it is not certain. The newspaper AS says Messi is a "doubt."

River Plate wants to sign Manchester United striker Radamel Falcao, but they admit the deal is difficult. Falcao played for River Plate for eight years before moving to Porto in 2009, and the club is open to him returning. Vice President Matias Patanian said, "We dream of Falcao Garcia. The doors are open." Falcao has had a hard time on loan at Manchester United.

Liverpool manager Brendan Rodgers says that his own experience of being rejected as a young player inspires him to give young players like Raheem Sterling and Jordon Ibe a chance in the first team.

Rodgers never became a professional footballer. He moved from Northern Ireland to England at age 16 to train with Reading’s youth team, but he did not succeed. He believes that remembering how it felt to miss out on a first-team spot—even after being promised one—helps him manage Liverpool’s young players.

Rodgers finds positive lessons in his failure to become a pro. As a result, 20-year-old star Raheem Sterling has thrived under his guidance.

On Tuesday, the Golden State Warriors beat the Los Angeles Clippers 110-106. This win was the Warriors' 10th game in a row. It also ended the Clippers' seven-game winning streak.

Stephen Curry scored 27 points for the Warriors, and Klay Thompson scored 25. David Lee added 17 points. The Warriors had lost four games in a row at the Staples Center before this win.

The Clippers had a 17-point lead but lost the game. Blake Griffin scored 40 points and got 12 rebounds. Chris Paul scored 27 points and made nine assists. J.J. Redick scored 14 points.

Stephen Curry was seen reacting after making a three-point shot against the Clippers

Former Liverpool player Jamie Carragher used the break in international matches to travel to Spain. He went there to watch his son, James, play for Liverpool’s Under-12 team in the Mediterranean International Cup. This well-known youth tournament takes place in Girona, in northern Spain, and includes more than 200 clubs from 36 countries. While in Girona, Carragher spoke with a local TV station and posted a photo of the opening ceremony on his Instagram account.

Finally, there is some good news for Sunderland and Newcastle United: in a local rivalry, past performance doesn’t matter. This is a relief because, on Sunday, both groups of fans can forget about their current struggles. In their last six games (12 matches total), the two teams have earned only six points. In those same 18 hours of play, they have scored just four goals together but have allowed 22 goals against them. It is no surprise that they call this game “The Desperation Derby.” Some might even say “The Donkey Derby” is a better name.

James Rodriguez, a star player for Real Madrid, will return to play against Granada on Sunday. He has been out for two months because he broke his right foot, but he is now healthy. The team’s manager, Carlo Ancelotti, said that Rodriguez practiced well and will start the game at the Santiago Bernabeu stadium. Rodriguez will play in the attack alongside teammates Cristiano Ronaldo and Gareth Bale.

Thiago, a key player for Bayern Munich, said it was an emotional moment to play in his first game in a year against Borussia Dortmund. He thanked the club for the opportunity.

Thiago had not played for Bayern since March 2014, when he suffered a serious knee injury. On Saturday, he came into the game to replace Philipp Lahm during Bayern’s 1-0 win at Westfalenstadion.

After seeing how the fans reacted, Thiago said it reminded him of how much he loves the sport. He stated, “Football is my life.” This was his first appearance in over a year.

St Etienne wants to sign Cardiff defender Kevin Theophile-Catherine permanently. The 25-year-old joined Cardiff from Stade Rennais for £2.1 million and has been on loan at St Etienne this season. St Etienne can buy him for £1.5 million, but Theophile-Catherine wants to look at other options before deciding. He still has two years left on his contract with Cardiff.

Meanwhile, St Etienne will not buy Norwich striker Ricky Van Wolfswinkel permanently. The Dutch player scored only one goal after his £8 million move.

Former Huddersfield player Josh Griffin scored one try and kicked three goals to help Salford win 18-12 against Huddersfield at the John Smith's Stadium. This victory gave Salford two wins in a row in the Super League.

Salford started the game quickly. In the first half, Griffin and Ben Jones-Bishop both scored tries. However, Jack Hughes scored for Huddersfield, giving them hope.

Later, Carl Forster scored a try for Salford, and Griffin kicked another penalty. These points made the win safe for Salford. Even though Huddersfield’s Aaron Murphy scored a try late in the game, Salford held on to win 18-12.

Salford player Rangi Chase might be banned from playing for four to eight games. He was charged with making a dangerous tackle (called a Grade E dangerous throw) during the Good Friday match against Huddersfield. Even though Salford won the game 18-12, they might lose Chase for a long time. The Rugby Football League’s review panel said his tackle on Brett Ferres in the 15th minute was dangerous. Chase has to appear before an independent disciplinary tribunal on Wednesday evening.

Andros Townsend seems to change more between being a top player and an under-achiever than anyone else. He is currently feeling good after scoring a great equalizing goal for England against Italy in Turin on Tuesday night. The 23-year-old Tottenham winger has had more highs and lows than most players do in their careers. When he plays well, he is as good as the best players. He scares defenders with his speed and direct style of play. He also shows this same confidence off the field, such as when he tweeted a "told you so" message to critic Paul Merson this week. People first noticed this ability two years ago when he tried to save his team, QPR, from being relegated by giving many excellent performances.

Warrington lost their third game in a row in the Super League and might get in trouble with the Rugby Football League because of crowd trouble during the match against Widnes. The game was paused for eight minutes after a fan threw a flare from the section where visiting supporters were sitting. Despite this, Widnes stayed focused and won 30-10. This win continues their strong performance at the Select Security Stadium, where they have earned seven points out of ten possible this year. Warrington’s losing streak is their worst since 2009. Their problems got worse when their winger, Matty Russell, hurt his leg. After the delay caused by the flare, Widnes secured Warrington’s third straight loss.

The England team has finally returned to England from Turin. Their flight was delayed, but it landed at Manchester Airport on Tuesday night after the 1-1 draw with Italy.

The team was supposed to leave northern Italy right after the game, but a problem with the plane forced Roy Hodgson’s players to stay one extra night.

The team stopped in Manchester so players and staff who live in the north could go home. Players from Manchester United, Manchester City, Everton, Liverpool, Aston Villa, and Stoke City left early to rejoin their clubs. They need to prepare for the Barclays Premier League matches this weekend.

Wigan moved up to third place in the Super League after beating their rivals, St Helens, to make up for losing the Grand Final in October. The Warriors won 12-4 in a very tough match in front of a full crowd of 24,504 people at the DW Stadium. Even though there were only three tries, the game showed rugby league at its best. The defenses were so strong that both teams were exhausted before the match ended. The game was intense, and the muddy field made it even harder. Wigan’s Dom Manfredi scored the first try for his team and celebrated with his teammates.

The Italian newspaper *La Gazzetta dello Sport* criticized Theo Walcott’s performance against Italy, saying he had very little impact. The newspaper rated England’s players out of 10. Walcott received the lowest score of five. England captain Wayne Rooney, goalscorer Andros Townsend, and substitute Ross Barkley all received a score of seven. Italy’s coach, Antonio Conte, was praised for leading his team to a 1-1 draw with England.

Daryl Clark, the current player of the year for the Warrington Wolves, will try to beat his former team, Castleford Tigers, when they play each other on Easter Monday. Castleford is having a difficult season, while Warrington is doing well.

Clark left Castleford last season to join Warrington. Even though he plays for a different team now, he still watches Castleford’s games closely. He said, “Castleford was the only team I played for when I was young, so it will feel strange to be on the other side.”

Clark is expected to play despite breaking his nose in a recent loss to Widnes. He wants to keep his record of playing every game for Warrington. He added, “I still check Castleford’s results

Brendan Rodgers, the manager of Liverpool, says that Raheem Sterling will stay at the club this summer. He is calm about the fact that Sterling has not yet signed a new contract.

Sterling, who is 20 years old, recently said in a TV interview that he is not ready to sign a new deal worth £100,000 a week. This comment made people think he might leave the club.

Rodgers said the interview was done without the club’s permission and that it surprised everyone. However, he also said that Sterling is still young and sometimes makes mistakes.

Joe Hart, a top goalkeeper for England, called Gianluigi Buffon a "legend of the game" after Buffon earned his 147th cap for Italy. Hart also reached a big milestone of his own by playing for England for the 50th time on Tuesday night. After the match ended in a 1-1 tie, Hart told FA TV that Buffon inspires him. He said, "I’m still learning my game and I’m still watching the likes of Buffon and the way he goes about his business at 37 years old." Hart, who plays for England and Manchester City, praised his fellow goalkeeper, Buffon.

Graziano Pelle, a 29-year-old striker for Southampton, has not scored many goals for his club recently. However, he proved that Italy coach Antonio Conte was right to trust him by scoring against England.

Pelle joined Southampton from Feyenoord for about £9 million. He did very well at first, scoring nine goals in his first 12 games. But in recent months, he has had trouble scoring. He has not scored in the Premier League since December 20.

On Tuesday night, at Juventus Stadium, Pelle helped Italy take the lead against England. He headed in a cross from Giorgio Chiellini into the far corner of goalkeeper Joe Hart’s net to make the score 1-0.

Five staff members were seriously hurt after riding the "Super Slide" at the Sydney Royal Easter Show on Saturday night. The slide had been closed because heavy rain made it too slippery and dangerous. Despite this, a group of eight workers broke into the 52-metre slide and went down it anyway.

On Saturday night, the English champions, Northampton Saints, were defeated by Clermont at the Stade Marcel Michelin. This loss highlights the big difference in money and power between English clubs and their wealthy French counterparts. It was a one-sided game that was a major disappointment for Northampton and for English rugby in general.

Although Northampton is leading the English league by 10 points, they were completely overpowered by Clermont, a top French team. Clermont is nearly unbeatable at home, and Northampton could not do anything to challenge them in this loud stadium.

Zara Tindall, 33, is a professional horse rider. Last September, she enjoyed playing wheelchair rugby, a sport often called "murder ball," at the Invictus Games. Now, she has tried barrel-pulling. She jokingly pretended to pull her husband, Mike, who is a 6-foot-tall rugby player weighing 16 stone, while posing for photos. This happened at a charity event celebrating the end of personal trainer Rob Edmond’s marathon barrel-roll, which took him from Perthshire to Wiltshire. Zara strapped herself into the harness used for pulling the barrel, while Mike sat on the barrel and smiled.

Manchester City manager Manuel Pellegrini says the club needs to sign young players because the players from their own youth academy are not yet ready to play in the first team. There have been rumors that City wants to sign Liverpool’s Raheem Sterling, who is currently stuck in contract negotiations with his current club.

Part of the reason City is looking for new young talent is a suggestion by Football Association chairman Greg Dyke. He wants to increase the number of homegrown players in Premier League squads to 12. Because of this, Pellegrini does not think the current young players at City are good enough to play alongside stars like Yaya Toure. The paragraph also notes that City goalkeeper Joe Hart was seen making a save during training on Wednesday.

Teachers are planning to vote on whether to go on strike this weekend. They are protesting against pay issues and working conditions, as well as potential cuts to school funding. If they vote to strike, tens of thousands of teachers could walk out in the autumn, which might cause schools to close temporarily. The National Union of Teachers, which has 300,000 members, will hold this vote after the election. If the vote passes, strikes could begin in September.

Nuri Sahin, who plays for Borussia Dortmund, says that Arsenal tried to sign him from the German league by offering a large amount of money. However, he did not move because his family wanted to stay in Germany.

Sahin, who is from Turkey and has previously played for Real Madrid and Liverpool, was interested by Arsenal back in 2005 when he was playing for Dortmund’s under-17 team. He told the news channel Ntvspor, "Arsenal wanted to sign me with a great bid. My family didn't want me to go to England."

He added, "They knew that Dortmund would rise again. I'm grateful for this. After the bid, Dortmund realized that I'm valuable."

Antonio Nuñez, 59, has been charged with aggravated assault after allegedly stabbing his girlfriend in the buttocks with a pitchfork. The incident happened at his home in San Antonio, Texas, on Monday morning.

According to police, the argument between Nuñez and the unnamed woman escalated around 4:15 a.m. Nuñez is accused of grabbing a gardening pitchfork and stabbing the woman. The woman managed to spray pepper spray in Nuñez’s eyes and ran across the street to a neighbor, who called 911. She is currently in the hospital recovering.

Tony Smith, the former coach for Leeds and England, was surprised when Kevin Sinfield decided to change sports, but he now thinks it might be a smart move. Sinfield, 34, is the best captain in Leeds' history. He shocked the rugby league world by announcing that he will stop playing rugby league at the end of the season. Instead, he will join Yorkshire Carnegie, a team connected to Leeds, for 18 months. Sinfield has scored 3,997 points, which puts him close to third place on the all-time scoring list for rugby league. At a press conference, he explained that he did not want to play against Leeds anymore. He also said that the chance to help Yorkshire Carnegie return to the top league was too good to pass up.

Surveillance video shows a man stealing a wild peacock from a neighborhood in Dallas, Texas. The residents of Beckley Club Estates say they saw the man grab the male peacock on Saturday around 7 p.m. The bird was showing off its feathers as part of its mating ritual when the man quickly picked it up. The video, recorded by resident Lisa Solis, shows the thief grabbing the bird by its feet and putting it into his black SUV.
These funny pictures show a male tortoise trying to mate with a female. He climbs onto her shell, but he loses his balance and falls onto his back. He fails to impress her, and she walks away.

A farmer filmed a sweet moment showing how a duckling and a lamb became friends. The video shows the lamb, named Winter, standing still in the sun with its head down near the baby duck. The duck walked to the front of the lamb and started pecking at its head and neck, acting like it was grooming its wool. The lamb kept its head lowered while the duck pecked, sometimes in a messy way. The lamb seemed to enjoy the attention, showing a clear sign of trust and friendship between the two animals.

A secret Cold War bunker in Chislehurst, a quiet suburb in southeast London, has been turned into a luxury home that is now for sale for £3.5 million. The building was designed and constructed in 1951 to protect government workers in case of a nuclear attack. It was built in a wooded area to keep it hidden and features five-foot-thick concrete walls.

Police are looking for three men who stole an ATM from a gas station in California last Friday morning. Video from a Shell station on Ygnacio Valley Road in Walnut Creek shows what happened. One man distracted the cashier at the window while another attached a cable from the back of a white pickup truck to the ATM. When the truck drove away, it pulled the machine out of the ground. Sparks flew as the heavy machine was dragged across the pavement. The man who had been talking to the clerk then ran to the truck.

Tyler MacNiven became famous after winning the ninth season of *The Amazing Race* and the $1 million prize. It looks like he used some of that money to make a special "save the date" video for his wedding.

Tyler and his fiancée, Kelly Hennigan, made a three-minute movie to let friends and family know about their upcoming wedding. They put a lot of effort into it. The video is inspired by action movies. In the film, the couple washes up on a beach, fights friends who are dressed as villains, and escapes a huge explosion. The video also tells everyone not to make plans for September 26, 2015, because that is their wedding day.

Veteran broadcaster Peter Alliss, 84, has caused controversy by saying that laws meant to ensure gender equality have actually hurt the game of golf. He argues that rules preventing golf clubs from discriminating against women have led to a drop in female membership. Before these rules, some clubs only let women join if they paid a lower fee and were allowed to play only at certain times.

In the past, winning a league title was the biggest success a manager could have, and it usually kept them in their job for many years. That is no longer true. Surprisingly, the last four managers who won the Premier League all left their jobs the following year—three were fired and one retired. Based on recent events, it would not be surprising if Manuel Pellegrini became the fifth manager to leave this summer. This follows Manchester City’s 2-1 loss to Crystal Palace on Monday night, which left Pellegrini looking disappointed. He had previously led City to their second Premier League title in three years in May.

During a press conference on Thursday, before Arsenal’s match against Liverpool, manager Arsene Wenger was confused by a journalist’s question. The confusion came from a fake news story published by MailOnline on April Fools’ Day. The story claimed that the team talks given by captains Per Mertesacker and Jordan Henderson would be broadcast live to everyone. Although the story was not true, it still caused a lot of confusion for Wenger and the reporters present.

Everton players Leighton Baines and Luke Garbutt visited Alder Hey Children’s Hospital on Wednesday to bring some Easter joy to the young patients and their families. After their training session, the two players gave out Easter eggs and took photos with the children in the hospital’s West Derby wards.

Baines said that while bringing chocolate eggs might seem small compared to how sick the children are, parents really appreciate the visit because it breaks up the routine of their day.

Oscar has been doing very well lately. The 23-year-old forward for Chelsea has won a Capital One Cup medal this season, and his team is currently leading the Premier League by six points. He also scored a goal in Brazil’s 3-1 win against France in Paris.

Before Chelsea’s game against Stoke on Saturday, Oscar posted a photo on Instagram showing him drinking from a bottle of sweets.

Carlisle United manager Keith Curle strongly criticized his team after they lost 3-1 to Accrington Stanley. He even suggested that some players do not deserve to be professional athletes. The team has not won a game in five matches in League Two. They are currently just two places and three points above the relegation zone. Speaking to BBC Radio Cumbria, Curle said the players showed a worrying lack of character. This criticism came after their poor performance in the match at the Crown Ground.

Jamie Carragher accused Yaya Toure of stepping aside when Jason Puncheon took a free-kick that ended Manchester City’s chances of getting a result at Selhurst Park. Toure, who earns £200,000 a week, was part of a five-player wall when Puncheon scored to extend Crystal Palace’s lead. However, Carragher, a columnist for Sportsmail, argued that Toure did not do enough to block the shot. Speaking on Sky Sports’ Monday Night Football, Carragher said, “That’s not acceptable when you go into a wall. The rest of them are desperate to be hit with the ball in the face, and it’s poor from Yaya Toure.”

Charlie Sumner, 20, has been banned from football for three years. The ban happened after he ran onto the field topless and did four front flips during his first game at the stadium.

The incident took place last month at Reading's Madejski Stadium during an FA Cup match against Bradford City. At the time, Reading was winning 3-0. Sumner landed on his back after each flip before security guards tackled him.

Mesut Ozil, who plays for Arsenal, posted a photo on Twitter showing him relaxing at home in London with his dog. He had just returned to the city after the international break.

Ozil played well in Germany’s 2-0 win over Georgia in their Euro 2016 qualifier on Sunday. Now, he is focusing on Arsenal’s upcoming match against Liverpool this weekend.

In the photo, Ozil shared a caption that said, "Home Sweet Home," giving fans a look at how he spends his free time.

Gerard Pique, a defender for Barcelona, said on Wednesday that Lionel Messi should be ready to play in Sunday’s La Liga match against Celta Vigo. This news comes despite concerns about a possible foot injury. Messi, who is the top scorer in La Liga, did not play in Argentina’s two friendly matches during the international break. He hurt his right foot during last month’s “Clasico” game against Real Madrid. Pique told reporters at a promotional event, “I am optimistic about Messi, I have spoken to him.”

FIFA announced that Greg Dyke, the chairman of the Football Association, has given back a £16,000 watch he received as a gift. The Brazilian Football Association gave him one of 65 limited-edition Parmigiani watches during a FIFA meeting in Sao Paulo at the World Cup. These watches were handed out in goodie bags worth more than £1 million. When FIFA asked for the watches back, Dyke first refused. He had promised to donate his watch to the charity Breast Cancer Care so it could be sold at auction.

Nottingham Forest manager Dougie Freedman says 18-year-old striker Tyler Walker could be the team’s main attacker for many years. On Monday, Walker came off the bench and scored his first senior goal against Brentford. This goal ties him with a Forest legend who shares his last name: his father, Des. Des scored only once in 408 games for the club. Tyler celebrated after scoring his first senior goal for Nottingham Forest in the away game against Brentford. It might be a funny topic at family dinners, but Tyler still has a long way to go to match his father’s record.

Peter Alliss, a well-known BBC golf commentator, said the BBC should have tried harder to get the rights to broadcast The Open Championship. He also argued that laws giving women equal rights in golf have caused chaos.

Recently, new laws have given women more rights in golf clubs. As a result, St Andrews and Royal St George’s have both voted to allow women to become members for the first time. However, Alliss told Radio Times magazine that this push for gender equality has "ruined the game for a lot of people."

Brad Fraser sang a funny song instead of giving a normal speech at his sister Amanda Beringer’s wedding. The wedding took place at Eagle Bay, south of Perth, over the weekend. Amanda asked Brad to speak because their father had passed away. Brad’s song made fun of the difficulties of marriage. He sang, “Well it's done now, you can't turn back. You're legally bound by the wedding trap.”

David Luiz might not be able to play for Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) in their upcoming Champions League match against Barcelona because he hurt his hamstring. This happened on Sunday during PSG’s 3-2 victory over Marseille.

Luiz had to leave the game after 35 minutes. He injured his left leg while running away from an opposing player. As he was carrying the ball out of defense, another player’s leg hit him. Luiz immediately signaled to the bench that he needed to be substituted.

A man in New Zealand was surprised to get a phone call from his brother, who had been missing for 10 years. John Daniel Tohill, 37, was last seen by his family in 2005 when he left Nelson on the Tasman Bay to travel north. On Tuesday evening, his brother Tobias received a call from John, who said he would visit in the coming weeks, according to Stuff NZ. This was the first time John had contacted his family since 2005. Over the years, his family hired investigators and the police, but because John was an adult and disappeared without notice, the police had little reason to ask the public for help.

A father is teaching his baby, Noah Monte, how to balance on his hand. YouTube videos show the four-month-old boy staying upright while being lifted up and down. Noah keeps his legs and body straight, and he uses his arms to help stay balanced. People watching can be heard laughing in the background. The father says Noah started doing this trick when he was only one month old.

Lucy Garrod, a 27-year-old photographer, was left almost blind in her right eye because of a bacterial infection under her contact lens. She had worn contacts without issues since she was 15, but one day she woke up with an itchy, irritated right eye. The bacteria caused an ulcer, called a corneal abrasion, which damaged her vision.

In preparation for tonight’s NCAA championship game, a group of meerkats at the Indianapolis Zoo in Indiana have been practicing their basketball skills. The zoo installed a makeshift backboard and hoop in their enclosure, and the animals were filmed inspecting the equipment and standing on their back legs. Instead of a flat court, they have to play on the uneven, hilly ground of their habitat. Visitors watched the animals with smiles, and the zoo also offered other Final Four activities over the weekend, such as a basketball-themed scavenger hunt.

In one home, a baby girl was excited by a toy hen instead of the Easter Bunny. A video from YouTube user Shkesi shows the baby watching the toy closely. The toy is a soft, motorized bird that bounces up and down and releases eggs. The baby is amazed by what she sees. She cries happily when the first egg comes out, and she screams with joy and waves her arms when the third egg appears. Before releasing the plastic eggs (not chocolate ones), the toy bird plays a short song that says, "I'm about to show you how it's done, laying eggs is so much fun."

A video shows a sudden snowstorm in Krasnoyarsk, Russia, which is the country’s third-largest city. The storm hit Siberia quickly, covering the Yenisei River and the Kommunalnyi Bridge in just seconds. Filmed from the riverbank, the footage shows what first looks like a large white cloud. This cloud is actually a fast-moving storm traveling at 45 mph. It grows larger and instantly covers the bridge, making the structure look small in comparison.

Dogs are usually very good at playing catch, especially when there is food involved. However, a video shows that Fritz, a Golden Retriever from California, does not have good eye-mouth coordination. In the video, Fritz is wearing bunny ears for Easter and tries to catch a hard-boiled egg with his teeth, but he fails. Slow-motion footage shows him licking his lips and jumping up enthusiastically to catch the treat. Even though he tries hard, the egg misses his mouth, bounces off his chest, and lands on the grass. Finally, Fritz looks sad with his head down and his bunny ears falling to the ground.

Loushanna and Shawn Craig from Birmingham, UK, went to Tenerife for a three-day holiday to celebrate Loushanna’s birthday and their anniversary. While they were there, thieves stole Loushanna’s passport ID card.

Because she no longer had her ID, Ryanair staff refused to let her fly home. They were worried she might be an illegal immigrant. As a result, Loushanna was stuck in Tenerife for up to two weeks.

Christopher Dodd, 24, and Fay Purdham, 27, are getting married. They grew up together as boys, playing football and video games. They lost touch as teenagers but reunited years later. At age 23, Fay transitioned to become a woman. They now live in South Bank, Middlesbrough, and are a couple.

Sir Nick Faldo will now know for sure if Rory McIlroy is getting too big after appearing to give the world’s number one golfer a squeeze during Monday’s practice round at Augusta National. McIlroy was recently on the cover of Men’s Health magazine and admitted he is “obsessed with the gym.” Faldo, who has won the Masters three times, expressed concern that the 25-year-old is spending too much time lifting weights. Last week, Faldo told the Daily Telegraph, “Throwing 200lb and 300lb weights around is not going to be good for your golf swing. The heaviest weight I would ever lift was my body weight.”

Three people survived after their hot air balloon hit a power line tower and crashed during a training flight in Russia’s Dmitrov district. Video shows the balloon hitting the side of the tower, causing the basket with the three people inside to fall to the ground. The instructor and two passengers were taken to the hospital with cuts and bruises, but they are all in stable condition.

Graeme McDowell admits that he has sometimes felt so frustrated by the difficulties of playing at Augusta National that he wished he could escape to a padded room. However, the former US Open champion is hopeful he can do better at this year’s Masters now that he has recovered from an ankle injury. This injury had forced him to quit the Valero Texas Open last month.

"It was the third time in my career that I had to withdraw from a tournament, and I don’t like doing that," McDowell said after practicing at Augusta. He added that he wasn’t sure how badly he had hurt his ankle at the time. In fact, he almost quit the pro-am event on Wednesday, and he thinks he probably should have.

Tiger Woods said he is ready to compete for his fifth Masters title after playing 11 holes of practice at Augusta National on Monday.

In 2015, Woods has only played in two tournaments. In the first, he scored 82, which was his worst score ever, and missed the cut. In the second, he withdrew after just 11 holes on February 5 because of an injury.

Because of these issues, the 14-time major champion took a break from competition to work on his game. During this time, he dropped out of the world’s top 100 for the first time since September 1996. On Monday, his ranking fell further, from 104th to 111th.

Notts County has hired Ricardo Moniz as their new manager. This happened just one week after the club said he could not take the job.

Moniz, who previously coached teams like Tottenham and Hamburg, withdrew from consideration in late March because of family reasons. However, on Tuesday, he moved to the club’s stadium, Meadow Lane, and signed a three-year contract.

The 50-year-old Dutchman now has six games left to keep his team from being demoted to League Two. Notts County is currently just one point away from safety.

An unknown person delivered chocolate eggs to every home in the village of Alderholt, Dorset, which has 3,000 residents. On Sunday morning, people woke up to find a chocolate egg on their doorsteps.

Rob Wood, 67, said it was a very kind gesture. He noted that every house in the village received one. He walked around the village and saw that everyone had received a chocolate egg wrapped in foil.

His daughter said that people were talking about it on Facebook. This has never happened before, and it must have been a large effort to deliver so many eggs.

Ben Crenshaw will make his 44th and final consecutive appearance in the Masters by replacing Arnold Palmer in the traditional par-three tournament at Augusta National. Palmer cannot play in the event on Wednesday afternoon along with Gary Player and Jack Nicklaus because he is recovering from a dislocated shoulder. However, the 85-year-old will still serve as the honorary starter on Thursday. Billy Payne, the chairman of Augusta National, stated in a press release: "We were sad to learn that Arnold will not participate in this year's Par 3 Contest, but his health is most important. Ben Crenshaw will join Jack Nicklaus and Gary Player in the par-three competition at the Masters."

Dundee manager Paul Hartley is not worried about Dundee United’s recent poor performance before their Scottish Premiership match on Wednesday at Dens Park. United have lost seven of their last nine games in all competitions and drawn two others. Their last league win was on January 24 against Motherwell. However, Hartley does not think this makes his team’s job easier. He wants to get his first win in a derby this season, which will be their fourth try. Hartley said, “They still have good players.”

Aston Villa manager Tim Sherwood has promised to ignore calls from his friend, Chris Ramsey, if Ramsey tries to call him before Tuesday’s important match. If Rangers win at Villa Park, they will move above Sherwood’s team and drop them back into the relegation zone. This game is very important for both teams. Ramsey, who was Sherwood’s close assistant at Tottenham last season, said he might try to call his former boss before the game. This match marks the first time Sherwood and Ramsey have faced each other as opposing managers.

Tomas Berdych beat Juan Monaco 6-3, 6-4 in the quarter-finals of the Miami Open on Wednesday. This win sets up a match against Andy Murray. It will be their first meeting since the Australian Open semi-final, which Murray won in four sets. That earlier match was tense and sometimes angry. Monaco fought hard in the second set, supported by many Argentine fans. However, Berdych broke serve to take a 5-4 lead and won the match.

Roger Federer, who is ranked number two in the world, is taking a break in the snow. He posted a photo on his official Twitter account showing him holding a snowball and his tennis racket. The 33-year-old included the funny caption "tennice" and was wearing a scarf from FC Basel, a soccer team he supports. His agent, Tony Godsick, said Federer chose not to play in the warm weather of the Miami Open this year to protect his physical health.

Exeter beat Newcastle 48-13 to reach the semi-finals of the first-ever European Challenge Cup. They will now play against Gloucester.

The game was played at Exeter’s home ground, Sandy Park. Exeter scored six tries to Newcastle’s one. David Ewers scored a try for Exeter, and they also got a penalty try. This helped Exeter lead 17-6 at halftime.

After halftime, Exeter scored more tries through Thomas Waldrom, Byron McGuigan, Sam Hill, and Dean Mumm. Newcastle managed only one try, scored by Chris Harris in the 68th minute. Newcastle also got eight points from Tom Catterick’s kicks.

During the match, Exeter’s Carl Rimmer was tackled by Newcastle’s

Lewis Ferguson received no special treatment at trainer Paul Nicholls’ stable on Thursday morning. The 18-year-old did his usual chores, such as cleaning the stables. He had only a small cut on his nose from a fall that has made him famous online.

On Wednesday, Ferguson fell from the favorite horse, Merrion Square, during the 4:20 pm race at Wincanton. The fall involved a double somersault and has been viewed hundreds of thousands of times on the internet.

Despite this, Ferguson was back riding horses. He said he was not discouraged from returning to riding. He explained, “It was just a blur. I didn’t understand what happened until I went back to the weighing room and watched the video replay.”

An Australian goanna was filmed eating a whole rabbit in less than one minute. The video shows the two-meter-long lizard balancing on top of a power pole while it swallows its prey. The lizard moves its neck back and forth as it struggles to eat, but it finishes in under a minute. The video starts by zooming in on the top of a tall power pole, where the goanna is sitting with the rabbit. In Aboriginal mythology, goannas are well-known. They can unhinge their lower jaws when they eat, which allows them to eat prey that is larger than their head.

Saracens chairman Nigel Wray called rugby’s salary limits "a farce" in financial papers seen by The Mail on Sunday. These documents show that the club’s spending on player wages went up by another £1 million last season, even though the team is currently being investigated for breaking salary cap rules.

This news comes two weeks after the club’s chief executive, Edward Griffiths, suddenly left his job, and three months after it was revealed that Premier Rugby was investigating Saracens for possible salary cap violations. The Mail on Sunday reports that Saracens’ total debt has now passed £40 million, which is the highest amount of debt ever seen in rugby history.

Liam Plunkett, a 29-year-old fast bowler for England, is targeting the West Indies batting team and is ready to use his speed to challenge them. He is back in contention for the Test series in the Caribbean after an injury ended his comeback last summer. Before that injury, he took 18 wickets in four Tests, playing a key role for England, a team often criticized for not bowling fast enough. Plunkett returned to the England team last summer during the series against Sri Lanka and India. He has now recovered from a minor ankle issue during Yorkshire’s pre-season trip to Abu Dhabi.

Martin Guptill has been called back to the New Zealand Test cricket team for a two-match series against England next month. Guptill scored 237 runs against the West Indies in the recent World Cup, but he has not played in a Test match for New Zealand since their tour of England in 2013.

Also selected is fast bowler Matt Henry. He played in the semi-final against South Africa and in the final against Australia, which New Zealand lost. This is Henry’s first time being called up to the Test team. The 23-year-old has played only 20 first-class matches so far.

England has only been in St Kitts for a short time, but it seems clear that they are ready to let Jonathan Trott try playing as an opening batsman again. Trott was England’s main player at number three for four years before he had to leave the 2013–14 Ashes series in Australia early due to stress. He was chosen for this three-Test tour of the Caribbean after working hard to get back into the team. Although many people were talking about Kevin Pietersen before the team left, the real focus of this tour will likely be on Trott, another batsman born in South Africa. The photo shows Trott practicing in the nets as he returns to international cricket, and he may be ready to play soon.

Eighteen months ago, England’s Test captain, Alastair Cook, thought Jonathan Trott’s international career was finished. Now, however, Cook believes Trott is ready to handle the intense pressure of playing again.

Trott’s career was interrupted during the 2013/14 Ashes series. He left the tour after just one match at the Gabba because he was struggling with what was first called a "stress-related condition" and later diagnosed as situational anxiety.

Cook was worried this would be the end of Trott’s time with the England team. But he has watched the 33-year-old rebuild his career with focus and determination. Trott did this first with his county team, Warwickshire, and then during a successful winter tour with the England

Barney Gibson, a cricketer from Yorkshire, has retired from the sport at age 19. He made his first-class debut in 2011, just 27 days after turning 15, which made him the youngest player in the history of county cricket. However, that was his only senior match. He never played for the main team again and only played for the second team (Second XI). In his final game for the second team, he did not bat or keep wicket; instead, he bowled three deliveries. Gibson said retiring was a difficult decision to make at such a young age.

The World Endurance Championship, which features the famous 24 Hours of Le Mans race, is stopping the use of "grid girls." These were women who posed next to the cars before races, often wearing very little clothing. Many people will support this change, while others who are used to seeing them may be upset. The series, supported by the FIA, is taking a more modern approach. The chief executive, Gerard Neveu, announced that starting at the next race at Silverstone, there will be no grid girls. This means the series will no longer have these models before any of its races.

Dr. Steve Peters, a well-known sports psychiatrist, says he only helped Jonathan Trott with the tools he needed to rebuild his career with the England cricket team. Trott, who plays for Warwickshire, arrived in the West Indies with England on Thursday night. This is his first time back with the national team since he left the Ashes tour last winter due to a stress-related illness. Trott has been open about his difficulties during that time, but he has slowly recovered his form playing for both Warwickshire and the England Lions. Now, he is close to returning to Test cricket.

Surrey has signed Australian all-rounder Moises Henriques to play in this summer's NatWest T20 Blast. He will join the team right after the Indian Premier League (IPL) ends next month. Henriques will stay with Surrey for the entire T20 Blast campaign. He will also serve as overseas cover for Kumar Sangakkara, depending on Sangakkara's Test match schedule in the second half of the summer.

Louis Smith has been named in the squad for the European Championships, marking his first time representing Great Britain since winning two medals at the 2012 London Olympics. At those Games, Smith won silver on the pommel horse and bronze with his team. After the Olympics, he focused on a career in media. Last year, he competed for England at the Commonwealth Games. He earned his spot on this team by winning gold on the pommel horse at the recent British Championships.

He will be joined by five other men: Max Whitlock, who won silver in the all-around and is the current pommel horse champion; and Olympic teammates Kristian Thomas, Sam Oldham, and Daniel Purvis. Courtney Tulloch completes the six-person team.

A three-meter-long python tried to eat a family cat but made a big mistake. Francis Bakvis found the python on Sunday while looking for his cat, Tiger, who had been missing for three days. Bakvis lives in Clifton Beach, in northern Queensland. He smelled a bad odor in his yard and saw a swollen python. Inside the snake were the remains of his cat. Most street festivals just grill some meat or roast a pig. But in one part of China, they roast a whole camel. The camel weighs 450kg (990lb). First, it is covered in a bright yellow sauce. Then, a crane lowers it into a giant oven that is 6 meters tall, according to People’s Daily Online. The camel is cooked inside the oven. After it is done, it is lifted out of the oven on a street in Jining, in northwest China.

The excitement for Sunday’s Manchester derby has officially begun. Radamel Falcao and Sergio Aguero, both from South America, appeared in a promotional video for Puma. In the video, titled "Head to Head," Falcao, who plays for Manchester United, and Aguero, who plays for Manchester City, compete in a cage-style match. Although this scene does not recreate the actual atmosphere of Old Trafford stadium, fans cheered as the two players were introduced. The fans were wearing the colors of their respective teams.

Dayna Dobias, a 19-year-old from Downers Grove, Illinois, has cerebral palsy. Instead of letting her disability hold her back, she dances and posts enthusiastic videos online to inspire thousands of people.

Dayna says her life has been difficult because she has been bullied and stared at by others. She hopes her videos will do more than just entertain; she wants them to inspire people to think before they judge. Her goal is to change how people with disabilities are shown in television, movies, and fashion.

Police say a 23-month-old girl died after her father accidentally ran over her with a pickup truck. The father did not see the child in the driveway.

Police were called to a home in North Las Vegas around 11:30 a.m. on Thursday. The father, 24, and other family members inside the house did not know the toddler had gotten out of the house and into the driveway. The girl later died at University Medical Hospital. This tragedy happened just days before her second birthday.

Police in Leesburg, Florida, arrested 23-year-old Lydia Kelm for driving under the influence. The incident happened early Monday morning at a McDonald’s drive-through.

According to police, Kelm arrived at the drive-through around 3:30 a.m. but did not pull up to the window. Instead, she caused a scene while wearing only a bra and panties. When officers tested her, her blood-alcohol level was .247.

Travis Hatfield, a 21-year-old aspiring country singer from Gilbert, West Virginia, became famous online after posting a video of himself singing to his uncle. Travis sang a George Jones song to his 47-year-old uncle, Jamie Joe Cline, who has Down syndrome.

Travis wrote on Facebook that his uncle is a very important part of his life and one of the sweetest people he has ever met. He said he didn’t know what he would do without him. Travis also shared the video to show people what he and his uncle do together on weekends. The video quickly became very popular on the internet.

Luis Figo, who is running for president of FIFA, said on Wednesday that the Confederation of African Football (CAF) was wrong to claim that all 54 African votes will go to the current president, Sepp Blatter. Figo was in Egypt at the CAF meeting to ask for support. He told Sportsmail that he does not believe all of Africa supports Blatter. Blatter is trying to stay in office on May 29. He is running against Figo, Prince Ali bin Al Hussein from Jordan, and Michael van Praag, who is the head of the Dutch football association.

This is a strange video showing a dog taking its owner for a walk. The footage, shared by a user named Vidsking on dailymotion.com, shows a large St. Bernard running across a road in the Czech Republic. A young boy is following behind the dog. Two men in a nearby car watch the scene and laugh. They have to slow down their car so they don’t hit the dog and the boy.

Everyone is watching Cristiano Ronaldo when Real Madrid plays Rayo Vallecano in La Liga on Wednesday. The 30-year-old scored five goals in Real Madrid’s big 9-1 win over Granada last weekend. This brings his total league goals to 36. His five goals put him ahead of Lionel Messi in the race for the Pichichi trophy, which goes to the top scorer in La Liga at the end of the season. The Spanish newspaper Marca previews Real Madrid’s trip to Rayo Vallecano on Wednesday night. The article focuses on the star forward, Cristiano Ronaldo, because of his five-goal performance against Granada. As the match approaches, Marca highlights Ronaldo.

Vincent Kompany says that if Manchester City can beat their rivals, Manchester United, in an away game, it will help fix their disappointing season. Manuel Pellegrini’s team had a tough match against Crystal Palace on Monday night. This loss basically ended their hopes of winning the Premier League title. Now, their only remaining goal is to finish in the top two. The City captain admits that this derby match is very important. He also believes that being the underdog works in their favor. Kompany thinks that beating Manchester United will help make up for a bad season. Meanwhile, manager Manuel Pellegrini is under pressure because of the team’s poor performance and might be replaced next summer.

Christian Benteke saved Aston Villa from being relegated by scoring a great free-kick late in the game. This goal completed his hat-trick and earned his team one point against Queens Park Rangers (QPR), who are also fighting to avoid relegation.

QPR’s Tim Sherwood’s team was about to fall into the bottom three positions when Charlie Austin scored his 17th goal of the season with 12 minutes left. However, five minutes later, Benteke scored to save the point and finish an exciting match.

Scottish golfer Bradley Neil, 19, has the support of world number one Rory McIlroy as he decides when to turn professional. Neil won the Amateur Championship at Royal Portrush last year, which earned him invitations to the 2015 Masters and US Open. The Walker Cup, taking place in September at Royal Lytham, is another key event on his schedule. Neil admits he might turn professional before that September match. He also impressed McIlroy during a practice round at Augusta on Monday. The video shows McIlroy practicing with Neil and congratulating him after Neil chipped in at the second hole.

If you planned to travel today to finish your Easter school break, you might wish you had stayed home. Thousands of people trying to leave Britain are facing serious problems because of two issues: strikes by French air traffic controllers and new border checks. These problems could cause delays of up to three days. Many airlines, including British Airways, easyJet, Ryanair, and Flybe, have had to cancel dozens of flights.

New York City police are looking for a man who was seen on a security camera dropping off an unconscious woman on a street in Queens over the weekend. On Tuesday, the police released the video and a photo of the victim, who is in the hospital, to help find her. The woman is seriously hurt and has not woken up. The blurry video, which a store owner in the Richmond Hill area of Queens gave to the police, shows a man wearing a hooded sweatshirt and sweatpants pulling the limp body of a woman from the backseat of a parked car at about 12:30 am on Saturday.

Peter Moores and Alastair Cook sounded frustrated when they answered questions about Kevin Pietersen’s future. This was more than a year after Pietersen seemed to be permanently removed from international cricket.

The only person to blame is Colin Graves, the incoming chairman of the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB). Graves has sent mixed messages, causing the England team to face major turmoil and internal rebellion.

Graves did a great job as chairman of Yorkshire, where he provided funding and improved the club. However, his early work in international cricket has been embarrassing.

Andy Murray will face Tomas Berdych in the semi-finals of the Miami Open. This is a rematch of their intense Australian Open semi-final in January, which Murray won. That previous match was so dramatic that even Murray’s girlfriend, Kim Sears, was heard swearing at Berdych.

In Miami, Murray will see two of his former staff members coaching his opponent. His former fitness trainer, Jez Green, and his former coach, Danny Vallverdu, both left Murray’s team to join Berdych’s.

Police say the knife attack that killed a young man outside a pizza store on Easter Monday might be connected to an earlier event. Reports suggest that Greg Gibbins had helped a woman who was being harassed earlier that night.

Mr. Gibbins and his friends were at The Beachcomber Hotel in Toukley, on the Central Coast of New South Wales, on Sunday night. Afterward, they went to a nearby restaurant, where Mr. Gibbins was stabbed in the chest.

Police have charged a 20-year-old man with murder. The victim was a talented football player. Investigations are still ongoing.

John Isner beat Japan’s Kei Nishikori, who was the fourth seed, with scores of 6-4 and 6-3 on Thursday. This win sent Isner to the semifinals of the Miami Open.

Isner, who is 6-foot-10 and known for his powerful serves, is the first American man to reach the semifinals in Miami since 2011.

In the match, Isner won the last eight points of the first set, breaking Nishikori when he had no points to end the set. He then took a 3-0 lead in the second set and did not face any serious challenges.

Phil Jones wants Manchester United to keep up their recent good play before Sunday’s big match against Manchester City. United will host City at Old Trafford. They are currently third in the league, just one point and one spot above City, with seven games left to play. This is the first time since November 23, 2013, that United has been ahead of City in the standings after playing the same number of games in a season. Jones hopes the team will play their best football against City. He started in United’s 3-1 home win over Aston Villa on Saturday.

On Thursday, Carla Suarez Navarro won her semi-final match against Andrea Petkovic with scores of 6-3 and 6-3. This victory moved her into the final of the Miami Open.

Suarez Navarro, who is the 12th seed from Spain, did not face a single break point during the match. She will play either Serena Williams (the top seed) or Simona Halep (the third seed) in the final on Saturday.

This is the eighth time Suarez Navarro has reached a WTA final, and she is hoping to win her second title. Petkovic, the 9th seed from Germany, lost to Suarez Navarro for the third time in their five meetings.

Lewis Ferguson, an 18-year-old amateur jockey, had no special treatment at trainer Paul Nicholls’s yard on Thursday morning. He cleaned the stables like everyone else. He only had a small cut on his nose from a fall that made him famous online.

Ferguson fell off his horse, Merrion Square, during a race at Wincanton at 4:20 pm. The horse was the favorite. The fall was a double somersault, and hundreds of thousands of people have watched the video online.

Despite this, Ferguson is back riding and is not afraid to get back on a horse. He said the fall happened so fast it was just a blur.

Rory McIlroy is eager for Thursday to arrive so he can try to win the Masters. If he wins, he will complete a "career grand slam," meaning he will have won all four major golf tournaments. He wants to join Gene Sarazen, Ben Hogan, Gary Player, Jack Nicklaus, and Tiger Woods, who have all achieved this.

Excitement about McIlroy’s goal has been growing since he won The Open at Hoylake last July. Although Tiger Woods returning to competition after a two-month break has taken some attention away from McIlroy, the world’s number one player is still focused on playing well. McIlroy says he has arrived at Augusta ready to make a strong effort to win.

O’Neill trains Shutthefrontdoor for his main owner, J P McManus. McManus also owns Jackdaws Castle and employs AP McCoy, a record-breaking jockey who is about to win his 20th straight jockeys’ championship before he retires.

Marcelo Bosch was celebrated by his teammates after kicking his team, Saracens, into the semi-finals of the Champions Cup in a dramatic match in north Paris. With strong wind blowing, Bosch kicked a 55-metre penalty in the final moments of the quarter-final against Racing Metro. This kick secured a 12-11 victory for Saracens at the Stade Yves-Du-Manoir.

The win was surprising because Saracens had been struggling for most of the game, but they showed great determination. Their victory means they will play against Clermont in St Etienne in two weeks.

Sussex head coach Mark Robinson says that wicketkeeper Matt Prior is still "pretty much out indefinitely" as he recovers from an Achilles injury. The 33-year-old had serious trouble with this injury last summer, which caused him to lose his spot on the England team to Jos Buttler. He has not played since July. Prior took time off to focus on getting better and admitted that his last game for England might have been his final one. Robinson’s update does not offer any good news.

On Sunday, Mark Selby, the world’s number one snooker player, won the Baic Motor China Open. He beat Gary Wilson 10-2 in the final match. Selby, who is from Leicester, won the best-of-19 match easily. This victory is his sixth ranking title and he won £85,000 in prize money.

Selby had won the German Masters in February. Earlier in this tournament, he had neck pain but still managed to beat Wilson. Wilson is ranked 55 places lower than Selby.

Selby won the first three frames of the match. Wilson then scored 91 points to win the fourth frame. After winning, Selby posed with his China Open trophy.

Marcelo Bosch, an Argentine player, helped his English team, Saracens, reach the semi-finals of the Champions Cup. He did this by kicking a penalty kick at the very last moment. The kick was successful, even though fans in the Colombes area were booing and whistling. After the kick, his teammates and coaches celebrated with him. This victory knocked Racing Metro 92 out of the competition. It was Bosch’s best moment since he started playing in Europe.

Steve Bruce has had worse weeks than this one. His week included photos of him diving by a pool and ended with a loss that suggests Hull City might be kicked out of the Premier League. This was a game they could not afford to lose, especially since their last seven matches include difficult games against Southampton, Liverpool, Arsenal, Tottenham, and Manchester United. However, they lost, extending their winless streak to five games and putting them in a difficult situation. Bafetimbi Gomis celebrated after scoring to give Swansea a 2-0 lead against Hull at the Liberty Stadium on Saturday.

Wisconsin defeated Kentucky 71-64, ending the Wildcats' chance to become the first college basketball team to go undefeated in nearly 40 years. Frank Kaminsky led Wisconsin with 20 points and 11 rebounds.

Wisconsin will now play Duke in the championship game at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis on Monday night. Duke beat Michigan State 81-61 in the earlier semi-final.

Wisconsin coach Bo Ryan said, "It gives us another 40 minutes." This victory marks Wisconsin's first trip to the final since 1941. After the game, Wisconsin players ran onto the court to celebrate, while Kentucky's perfect season came to an end.

Harry Kane played very little in the match against Burnley, but he still helped his manager, Mauricio Pochettino. Kane’s role as captain distracted people from Tottenham’s poor performance and the fact that their chances of reaching the Champions League are now very slim. This helped avoid negative headlines about the team’s struggles.

Kane was the captain for Tottenham Hotspur in their Premier League game against Burnley at Turf Moor. At 21 years and 251 days old, he became the youngest Premier League player to serve as captain this season.

As a former world champion, Daley knows he must try harder to improve his sport. He spent most of last year trying to master this difficult dive, which he calls his "demon" dive. It is a confusing mix of flips and twists that he hoped would give him an advantage.

Ryuichi Kiyonari set a new lap record at Donington Park to earn the first starting position, or "pole," for the first race of the MCE British Superbike Championship on Easter Monday. Riding for Buildbase BMW, the Japanese rider completed the lap in 1 minute and 29.455 seconds. He beat James Ellison, who rides for JG Speedfit Kawasaki, by just 0.029 seconds.

Shane Byrne, the current champion, also made it to the front row of the starting grid. He rides for PBM Kawasaki. Despite this, Byrne is still recovering from hand and ankle injuries he got last month during testing in Spain.

Esteban Cambiasso has won every major soccer competition in Europe during his long career. However, he says that keeping Leicester City in the Premier League would be one of his greatest achievements.

Leicester City is currently at the bottom of the league table, seven points behind safety, with only eight games left to play. Time is running out for them to avoid being relegated.

Cambiasso refuses to give up. He says that saving Leicester’s place in the league would feel just as good as winning a trophy. He told BBC East Midlands Today, "For me, it's like another cup."

Sportsmail and Gillette are giving one reader the chance to win a pair of Nike Magista Obra soccer boots signed by Joe Hart. Hart is the goalkeeper for England and Manchester City. This is a rare chance to own memorabilia signed by one of the best players in the world.

Because Hart works with Gillette, the winner will also get a new Fusion ProGlide razor with Flexball technology (worth £12) and a bottle of Gillette Fusion ProGlide shave gel (worth £4.99). The contest ends on Sunday, April 19. Click here to enter for a chance to win.

Southampton striker Graziano Pelle says he is still confident, even though he hasn’t scored in the Premier League since December 20. The 29-year-old recently scored for Italy in a 1-1 friendly against England on Tuesday. He hopes to get back to his earlier form, when he scored eight goals in his first 17 league games. Pelle thanked the fans for supporting him during this difficult period, and manager Ronald Koeman believes he can score more goals in the final eight games of the season. Despite not scoring in his last 13 Premier League matches, Pelle remains confident.

Rangers manager Stuart McCall says Walter Smith warned him not to take the job at Ibrox, but he believes he made the right choice. McCall, a former player for the team, led Rangers to their third straight win with a 2-1 victory over Hearts on Sunday. This important win puts Rangers back in second place in the Scottish Championship and gives them strong momentum for the play-offs at the end of the season. Although he was advised against taking the job, McCall is happy he took the risk. Since taking over a month ago, he has united the players and quickly turned them into strong candidates for promotion.

Catalans Dragons have received bad news because winger Vincent Duport will miss the rest of the season due to a shoulder injury. The French player, who scored three tries in the first six games of Super League XX, tore a tendon during the team's 33-22 loss to Hull FC on March 20. He needs surgery for the injury.

Catalans head coach Laurent Frayssinous said the news is very disappointing for both Duport and the team. However, the coach added that Duport has recovered from serious injuries before and is sure to come back stronger.

Former Sunderland defender Danny Higginbotham called Roy Keane’s speech "one of the strangest team talks I’ve ever heard." This happened during the 2007-08 Premier League season, just before Sunderland played Aston Villa. Keane gathered his players in the home locker room at the Stadium of Light. Instead of telling them to forget their bad start to the season, he gave them a shocking speech. The text also notes that Roy Keane, who was the assistant manager for the Republic of Ireland, looked frustrated during a draw with Poland.

Manchester City has not won a Premier League game after being behind at halftime in nearly 20 years. This statistic comes after City’s title hopes were damaged by a 2-1 loss to Crystal Palace on Monday night. Manuel Pellegrini’s team was trailing at halftime. The last time City won a game after being behind at halftime was on April 17, 1995, when they beat Blackburn Rovers 3-2, despite being down 2-1 at the break. After the loss, Manchester City captain Vincent Kompany and goalkeeper Joe Hart walked off the field.

On Friday, Memphis beat Oklahoma City 100-92. This win tied Memphis for second place in the NBA’s Southwest Division. The Grizzlies’ defense stopped Oklahoma City’s star player, Russell Westbrook.

Memphis is now tied with Houston for second place in the division. Both teams are behind Golden State, which has already won the conference title.

San Antonio stayed within two games of second place by beating Denver easily.
